It is submitted that the case is still under investigation and the case record is lying with the Chief Judicial Magistrate, but he is not legally authorized to entertain bail petition in the case under Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Ain 2000. As such, the accused petitioner has not other option but to surrender before this Court for anticipatory bail. 

 4. It is true that Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Ain 2000 is a special law and section 19(2)(3) thereof relates to the power of granting bail by the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Tribunal alone but such power can only be exercised when the Investigating Officer submits police report in respect of any offence under the said Ain, 2000 and the Tribunal takes cognizance under section 19(1) read with section 27 of the Ain 2000. Prior to the taking of cognizance by the Tribunal, the F.I.R. case is treated as G.R. Case for the simple reason that during investigation, it cannot be identified as Nari-O-Shishu case with certainty. If the G.R. case is ultimately found to be one under any of the provisions of the Penal Code or any other law not triable by the Tribunal, then disposal of bail application of the accused by the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Tribunal becomes without jurisdiction. 

 5. Under section 61 of the Code of Criminal Procedure a person arrested under such G.R. case, irrespective of the fact that allegation is made under the offence of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Ain 2000, is to be produced before the Magistrate within 24 hours and such Magistrate is authorized either to allow remand under section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, send him to jail custody or grant him bail under section 497 thereof invoking general authority given to him under the scheme of the Code of Criminal Procedure. This is because during investigation such P.I.R. case cannot be treated as Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon case which shall be treated as such only after taking cognizance by the Tribunal. A criminal proceeding under the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Ain 2000 commences from the time when cognizance is taken by the Tribunal. The Tribunal Judge does not come in the seisin of the matter before the stage of taking cognizance to exercise power of granting bail under section 19(2)(3) of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Ain 2000 for the reasons stated above. During investigation of G.R. Case, even if allegation is brought under Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Ain 2000 on refusal of granting bail by the Magistrate, the accused shall be entitled to pray for bail by filing Misc. case under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Court of Sessions. Such power of the Sessions Judge cannot be exercised by the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Domon Tribunal in any way, because section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is neither a procedural law for holding trial nor such power of granting bail is available to the Tribunal within the meaning of section 25 of the Ain, 2000. It May be noted here that similarly, power of the Sessions Judge under section 435/439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be exercised by the Tribunal within the meaning of section 25 of the Ain, 2000. So, we hold the view that there is no legal 

 bar to entertain a bail prayer and to make disposal of the same by the Magistrate so long it remains a G.R. Case, and before taking of cognizance by the Tribunal as a Nari-O-Shishu Nil Domon Tribunal, it has no jurisdiction to deal with bail matter in such G.R. Case like the Magistrate or Sessions Judge. 

 7. Accordingly, the accused-petitioners namely- 1) Fazlur Rahman, son of late Mainuddin Shaik, 2) Halima Khatun, wife of Mainuddin Shaik, 3) Mainuddin Shaik, son of Majid Munshi, 4) Shoma Akhtar, wife of shafiqul Islam, 5) Shajhan Shaikh, son of Mainuddin Shaik and 6) Minara, wife of Shajhan Shaik, are directed to surrender before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Munshigonj within 2(two) weeks from the date in connection with Munshigonj P.S. Case No.27 dated 22.9.2008 under section 1 1 (Ga)/30 of the Nari-O-Shishu Nirjaton Damian Ain, 2000, now pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Munshigonj. 

 8. During this period, the police authority is directed not to arrest them in connection with the aforesaid case. After their surrender within the specified time, the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Munshiganj shall be at liberty to consider their bail application, if any, on merit and in accordance with law.
